I loved that everything was already booked and paid for, which made the trip stress-free and convenient.

The complimentary massage and pool access at the hotel were especially appreciated after long days and wedding activities.

about.heading: Travel, with a little more you.
about.body: Travel with Ease is Accra's boutique travel planning agency for people who want to travel well without the burden of planning. Whether it's your first trip abroad or your fifteenth, we handle the flights, hotels, itineraries and support, so you don't have to. First-timers get a patient guide. Busy travellers get their time back.

entries.heading: Founded by Nana Abena Osei-Wusu
entries.text: I grew up travelling every year, thanks to my parents. As I got older, the roles reversed: I was the one filling in passport and visa forms, booking flights and hotels, and planning trips for my parents and me. Then I started exploring on my own. Without realising it, I was always researching and planning great trips, and I never thought of it as a business. I love planning, and I love structure. I wanted to build something alongside my career, and when I put my ideas down, everything came back to travel.

articles.title: 6 documents every Ghanaian traveller needs
articles.excerpt: Check these before you book, and again before you fly.
articles.body:
1. Valid passport. Check your expiry date. Many countries want at least 6 months' validity beyond your travel dates, not just the day you fly out. Check your destination's rule.

2. Visa or entry approval. Check the requirements before you book. Some visas take weeks to process, so apply early.

3. Yellow fever certificate. Travellers aged 9 months and older need it to enter Ghana, and many destinations ask for it too. The vaccine must be given at least 10 days before travel. With no certificate on your return, you can be vaccinated at the airport at your own cost.

4. Return ticket. Airlines and immigration may ask for proof that you are leaving. Have it ready at check-in.

5. Proof of accommodation. Keep your hotel booking confirmation to hand. Immigration may ask where you are staying.

6. Travel insurance. It covers medical emergencies, cancellations and lost luggage. Some destinations, such as Kenya and Zanzibar, now require it.

Entry rules change. Confirm with the embassy or an official source before you travel. Last checked October 2026.

articles.title: What to expect at Accra International Airport
articles.excerpt: Four things to get right before you reach the check-in desk.
articles.body:
1. Arrive early. Aim to arrive at least 3 hours before an international flight. That gives you time for check-in, security and any unexpected delays.

2. Keep your documents ready. Keep your passport and booking details within reach. You will show them at check-in, at immigration and at boarding.

3. Know your entry requirements. Check your destination's visa and entry rules in advance. Missing documents are a common reason for being denied boarding.

4. Pack smart. Follow your airline's rules on liquids, electronics and essentials in your hand luggage, and keep what you need for the flight within easy reach.

Entry rules change. Confirm with the embassy or an official source before you travel. Last checked October 2026.

articles.title: Know why you could be denied boarding
articles.excerpt: Most reasons are avoidable if you check before you fly.
articles.body:
Why it happens

- Your passport has less validity than your destination requires, often 6 months
- Not enough blank pages left in your passport
- No visa, eVisa or ETA
- No yellow fever card, if required
- The name on your ticket doesn't match your passport
- An overbooked flight, which is the airline's fault

If you're turned away at the desk

- Stay calm and polite
- Ask why, and get it in writing
- If the flight is overbooked, ask for the next flight
- If the flight is overbooked, ask what compensation or support the airline offers
- Keep your boarding pass and receipts
- Screenshot your booking

Entry rules change. Confirm with the embassy or an official source before you travel. Last checked November 2026.

articles.title: Visa-free doesn't mean what you think
articles.excerpt: Ten myths that catch Ghanaian travellers out.
articles.body:
1. "Visa-free means I can just show up." It means no visa application in advance. It doesn't mean no questions at the border. Officers can still question you, check your documents and refuse entry if something is missing. Arrive with your full document set.

2. "My passport is valid, so I'm fine." Many countries require at least 6 months' validity beyond your return date, not just your travel dates. A passport expiring in 3 months could get you denied boarding before you leave Accra. Check your expiry before every trip.

3. "I don't need a return ticket." Many visa-free destinations ask for proof of onward travel. If you can't show a return or connecting flight, you can be turned away at the border, even if you have the right to enter. Book your return before you travel.

4. "I don't need a yellow fever certificate." Ghana is on the WHO yellow fever risk list, and many countries ask for the certificate on arrival. Without it you can be quarantined, fined or sent back, whatever your visa status. Keep your yellow fever card with your passport. Always.

5. "Visa-free means the whole journey is visa-free." Your destination may be visa-free but your layover country might not be. Connecting through the US, the UK or certain Schengen countries can require a transit visa, even if you never leave the airport. Check your transit country, not just your destination.

6. "The airline will let me board." Airlines check your documents before you board, not just the destination country. They are fined for carrying passengers who are refused entry, so they are strict. If your paperwork is incomplete, you won't make it onto the plane. Have every document ready before you reach the airport.

7. "Visa on arrival is the same as visa-free." It isn't. You still need a visa. You just get it when you land instead of applying in advance. It usually costs money, often payable in USD cash, so know the fee and how to pay before you fly.

8. "Visa-free means no money checks." Some countries check that you can fund your stay, and some travellers have been asked at check-in in Accra to show cash or pay a refundable deposit. Research your destination's financial requirements, and keep proof of funds ready. Check-in is not the place to find out.

9. "I just need my passport and ticket." Some countries require an online health declaration or arrival form before you travel, separate from your visa. Arriving without it can delay or deny your entry. Research your destination's pre-arrival requirements, not just its visa status.

10. "I can figure it out when I get there." By the time you're at the airport, it's too late. Missing documents, the wrong visa type and an expired yellow fever card can't be fixed at the check-in counter. That is why the Travel Readiness Session exists. We walk you through the requirements for your destination before you book anything.

Entry rules change. Confirm with the embassy or an official source before you travel. As at July 2026.

articles.title: Visa myths: visa-free, visa on arrival and eVisa
articles.body:
Myth: Visa-free and visa on arrival are the same thing. Fact: Not quite. Visa-free means no visa is needed at all. Visa on arrival means you do need one, and you get it, and pay for it, when you land.

Myth: An eVisa is something you sort out when you arrive. Fact: No. You apply online before you travel and arrive with it already approved. Leave it too late and you may not fly.

Myth: If a country is visa-free, there's no paperwork at all. Fact: You may still need a return ticket, proof of funds, a hotel booking or a yellow fever card, and an airline can deny you boarding without them.

Myth: An ETA is just another word for a visa. Fact: It isn't a visa. It's online permission to travel that some visa-free countries now require, for example Seychelles. Visa-free, but not paperwork-free.

Confused? That's normal. Knowing exactly what your passport needs is my job.

Entry rules change. Confirm with the embassy or an official source before you travel. As at August 2026.

articles.title: A few things I wish I'd known before Kenya
articles.excerpt: Small things that make a big difference in Nairobi.
articles.body:
1. It's visa-free for Ghanaians, with no eTA. You can stay up to 90 days and be cleared at the border, with nothing to apply for beforehand. Immigration will ask for three things: your return ticket, how long you're staying and where you're staying. (As of August 2026. Rules change, so check before you fly.)

2. Travel insurance is now compulsory. Kenya requires visitors to have it, and it costs about US$44 per person. Plan for it before you fly, not at the airport. Booking a Travel with Ease package? It's included.

3. Sort your data before you leave arrivals. Buy a SIM at the airport or set up a travel eSIM in advance. Once you leave the terminal you may lose Wi-Fi, and you'll want data to find or contact your Uber.

4. Uber and Bolt both work well. They are easy and affordable, and there's no haggling over taxi fares in Nairobi.

5. The expressway isn't free. It's faster and traffic-free, so your driver may ask whether to take it, and the toll is added to your trip. It's cash or M-Pesa only. If you pay Uber by card, the driver can cover the toll and you settle up in the app.

6. Some places are fully cashless. Kenya leans heavily cashless. Register M-Pesa on a Safaricom SIM at the airport to pay like a local, or bring a card that works internationally. Keep a little cash for tolls and tips.

7. Flying out? Leave extra time. On the way to JKIA, your car stops at a checkpoint before the terminal. Everyone gets out for screening, then gets back in. It catches people off guard, so don't cut your airport arrival too fine.

8. Pack your yellow fever certificate. Travelling from Ghana, it's commonly required for entry. It's easy to forget and a real problem without it.

9. Kenya is colder than you'd expect. Nairobi sits high up, so mornings and evenings get chilly, especially around August. Pack layers and a jacket. It's not the East Africa most people picture.

privacy.body: Travel With Ease uses your information to respond to enquiries, provide the travel services you request and operate this website.

entries.heading: Who handles your information
entries.text: Travel With Ease, a trading name of TWE Concierge, is based in Accra, Ghana. Contact nana@travelwitheasegh.com or +233 20 020 9170 with questions about your information.

entries.heading: Information you provide
entries.text: The enquiry form collects your name, email, WhatsApp number, enquiry type, requested service, destination, travel timeframe, number of travellers, optional budget, a yes or no visa-status answer where relevant, and your permission to respond. It does not ask for general notes, visa details, passport information, payment details or medical records.

entries.heading: Operational and security information
entries.text: We store your enquiry reference, submission and notice timestamps, source, delivery status and the staff actions needed to manage your request. Hosting and security providers can process IP addresses, browser/request metadata and security events. Cookie preferences are stored in your browser.

entries.heading: Why we use it
entries.text: We use your details to assess your request, contact you, prepare agreed travel services and protect the service. Enquiry consent is not marketing consent. Where processing relies on consent, you can withdraw it by contacting us; withdrawal does not undo processing already carried out.

entries.heading: Analytics and search
entries.text: Optional Google Analytics is blocked until you allow analytics cookies and remains subject to browser privacy signals. It measures public website usage, not enquiry answers or private staff activity. Google Search Console provides search-performance information separately from the analytics tag.

entries.heading: Providers and communications
entries.text: Cloudflare and Railway provide hosting, storage or security; Resend handles operational email; Google supports optional analytics, search reporting and approved media-source operations. Production enquiry acknowledgements copy notifications@travelwitheasegh.com so the team can respond. WhatsApp, Instagram and TikTok links open third-party services with their own terms. Provider processing can take place outside Ghana.

entries.heading: Retention and access
entries.text: We keep information for handling your enquiry, agreed services and applicable legal or dispute requirements. Authorised staff access is restricted by role. Contact us about retention or deletion; some records may need to be kept where an applicable obligation requires it.

entries.heading: Your choices and rights
entries.text: You can contact us to request access, correction, deletion where applicable, raise an objection or withdraw consent. We may need proportionate identity verification. You can also contact Ghana’s Data Protection Commission at https://dpc.gov.gh about your rights under the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843).

entries.heading: Effective date
entries.text: 1 November 2026. Material changes to this notice will be reflected here.

terms.heading: Booking and planning terms
terms.body: Read these terms alongside your live quote before making a payment.

entries.heading: Planning services and payment
entries.text: Complete the intake and pay 50% of the planning fee, or 60% for group planning, to begin. We confirm the start date by WhatsApp. The balance is due before the final travel pack is delivered.

entries.heading: Your Travel Fund
entries.text: Travel costs are separate from the planning fee. We send a Travel Fund Request for the exact booking costs and book only when funds have cleared. We do not advance booking costs. Foreign-currency estimates include a 5% buffer; any unused buffer is refunded.

entries.heading: Revisions and scope
entries.text: Full Trip Planning includes one minor revision; further minor revisions cost GHS 150 each. Premium includes unlimited minor revisions. A new destination or full itinerary restructure is a new scope. Planning fees are fixed.

entries.heading: Group changes
entries.text: Group changes cost GHS 100–150; date changes cost GHS 150. Supplier cancellation terms and actual cancellation costs also apply.

entries.heading: Package prices
entries.text: Published "from" prices are indicative, per person sharing a room, and include return flights from Accra. They are based on our reference month. Your final price depends on your travel dates, hotel availability, live airfare and the exchange rate. We send you a live quote before you pay a deposit. If your balance is due months after booking, it is recalculated at the exchange rate on your final payment date.

entries.heading: Package deposits and balances
entries.text: A GHS 5,000 deposit per person confirms your package booking and locks the quoted rate, subject to the exchange-rate provision above for a later balance. This deposit is non-refundable if you withdraw. The balance is due on the date in your quote, normally 45–70 days before departure depending on the hotel. Bookings are made only after funds have cleared. Payment is available through Telecel Cash or MTN MoMo; payment instructions are provided privately.

entries.heading: Insurance and travel documents
entries.text: Packages include the insurance specified in their inclusions. You remain responsible for your passport, visas and entry requirements; advice is not a visa guarantee. For planning-only services, travel insurance is recommended. Entry and insurance rules can change, so confirm the current requirements before travel.

entries.heading: Room sharing
entries.text: A single supplement applies when you do not share a room. Message us for your exact price.

entries.heading: Display currency and indicative exchange rates
entries.text: The website currency selector changes display estimates only. Package and service prices are published in Ghanaian cedi (GHS); original GHS amounts remain alongside conversions. Reference rates are supplied by ExchangeRate-API and cached, so conversions are approximate, not a live quote, bank rate, payment-currency choice or price guarantee. The selector's accessible status and tooltip identify the rate date and any cached fallback. Rates over 72 hours old are not used; if a rate is unavailable or expires, the website shows GHS. Changing display currency does not change your quote, booking terms, payment schedule, or the separate Travel Fund exchange-rate provisions above. Your successful currency preference is stored on this browser under twe-display-currency-v1; clearing browser storage resets it. Currency switching requires JavaScript, but original GHS prices remain available without it.

how-it-works.heading: How it works
how-it-works.body: A clear plan, a live quote and no bookings until your funds have cleared.
how-it-works.seoTitle: How it works | Travel With Ease
how-it-works.seoDescription: Learn how TWE package bookings and personalised trip planning work, including quotes, deposits and booking terms.

image.alt: A safari vehicle at the East Gate entrance to Nairobi National Park.

steps.heading: Choose your package
steps.text: Pick your package, tier, dates and number of travellers, then send them through the enquiry form or DM EASE. No budget needed.

steps.heading: Review your live quote
steps.text: We send a live quote for your exact dates, held for 14 days. Check the dates, hotel tier, inclusions and exclusions before you agree.

steps.heading: Confirm with a deposit
steps.text: A GHS 5,000 deposit per person confirms your booking and locks your rate. The deposit is non-refundable if you withdraw. Your balance is due on the final payment date in your quote, usually 45 to 70 days before departure.

steps.heading: Travel
steps.text: You receive your itinerary and travel pack, and we support you through the trip.

steps.heading: Travel with your pack
steps.text: You receive your travel pack with all your confirmed bookings, and we walk you through it on WhatsApp before you go.

package.example: Two friends considering 3 nights and 4 days in Nairobi send their preferred travel month, two travellers and the package they like. They compare the hotel tiers against the live quote, review the payment schedule, confirm with their deposit and receive their itinerary.

exampleSteps.heading: Start with the Nairobi package
exampleSteps.text: Two friends choose the 3-night, 4-day Nairobi package, share their preferred month, confirm two travellers and select the hotel tier they want to explore.

exampleSteps.heading: Compare the live quote
exampleSteps.text: They check their exact dates, accommodation options, inclusions and exclusions, then ask about room sharing and any extras before agreeing.

exampleSteps.heading: Confirm the booking
exampleSteps.text: They review the 14-day quote and payment schedule, then each pay the GHS 5,000 deposit to confirm. Their quote states when the remaining balance is due.

exampleSteps.heading: Get ready for departure
exampleSteps.text: They receive their itinerary and travel pack, check their travel arrangements and use the support included in their package.

steps.heading: Tell us about your trip
steps.text: Complete the planning questionnaire with your destination ideas, dates, travellers and budget.

steps.heading: Start planning
steps.text: Pay a deposit of 50% of your planning fee (60% for group trips). We confirm your planning start date, then build your day-by-day itinerary and budget. Full Trip Planning includes one revision. Premium Concierge includes unlimited minor revisions.

steps.heading: Fund your bookings
steps.text: We send a Travel Fund Request for the exact cost of your flights and hotels, separate from our planning fee. We book only once your funds have cleared.

steps.heading: Receive your travel pack
steps.text: Your planning balance is settled first, then you receive your final travel pack.

planning.example: A couple planning an anniversary in Italy complete the questionnaire with their dates and budget. They pay the planning deposit, review their day-by-day plan and ask for one change. They then fund their flights and hotels through the Travel Fund Request, and receive their travel pack before they fly.

exampleSteps.heading: Share the anniversary plans
exampleSteps.text: A couple describe their Italy anniversary trip, including preferred dates, destinations, travellers and approximate budget in the planning questionnaire.

exampleSteps.heading: Start the itinerary
exampleSteps.text: They pay the 50% planning-fee deposit, receive their proposed day-by-day itinerary and budget, and request one revision under Full Trip Planning.

exampleSteps.heading: Fund the bookings separately
exampleSteps.text: After reviewing the plan, they receive a Travel Fund Request for flights and hotels. Bookings proceed only after those funds have cleared.

exampleSteps.heading: Receive the final travel pack
exampleSteps.text: They settle the balance of the planning fee and receive their travel pack with their final arrangements before departure.

cookies.heading: Cookies and preferences
cookies.body: Choose whether to allow optional analytics. Essential security and preference storage remain available without analytics consent.

entries.heading: Essential storage
entries.text: The public website stores your preference under twe-cookie-consent-v1 in your browser. Separate protected cookies support staff sign-in and security. These are not public marketing preferences.

entries.heading: Optional analytics
entries.text: If you choose analytics, the configured Google Analytics tag can measure public website usage and set identifiers such as _ga. It is not loaded before consent. Cookie names and expiry behaviour depend on the active Google configuration.

entries.heading: Change your choice
entries.text: Use Cookie settings in the footer to review your preference at any time. Essential only does not grant analytics consent. Changing preferences stops future optional measurement; it does not remove information already processed.

entries.heading: Other services
entries.text: Google Search Console is separate search reporting, not a cookie category enabled by this popup. Following an external WhatsApp or social-media link takes you to that service’s own privacy and cookie rules.
